records.claim: The proposed approach encodes the input sentence into a sequence of vectors and chooses a subset adaptively, rather than encoding the whole sentence into a single fixed-length vector.

records.claim: Standard language models are unidirectional, which limits the choice of architectures that can be used during pre-training.
records.quote: The major limitation is that standard language models are unidirectional, and this limits the choice of architectures that can be used during pre-training.

records.claim: Unidirectional restrictions are sub-optimal for sentence-level tasks and could be very harmful for token-level tasks like question answering where bidirectional context is crucial.
records.quote: Such restrictions are sub-optimal for sentence-level tasks, and could be very harmful when applying fine-tuning based approaches to token-level tasks such as question answering, where it is crucial to incorporate context from both directions.

records.claim: BERT alleviates the unidirectionality constraint by using a “masked language model” (MLM) pre-training objective.
records.quote: BERT alleviates the previously mentioned unidirectionality constraint by using a “masked language model” (MLM) pre-training objective, inspired by the Cloze task Taylor (1953) .

records.claim: The MLM objective enables the representation to fuse the left and the right context, allowing pre-training of a deep bidirectional Transformer.
records.quote: Unlike left-to-right language model pre-training, the MLM objective enables the representation to fuse the left and the right context, which allows us to pre-train a deep bidirectional Transformer.

records.claim: BERT uses masked language models to enable pre-trained deep bidirectional representations, unlike Radford et al. (2018) which uses unidirectional language models.
records.quote: Unlike Radford et al. (2018) , which uses unidirectional language models for pre-training, BERT uses masked language models to enable pre-trained deep bidirectional representations.

records.claim: BERT uses masked language models, in contrast to Peters et al. (2018a) which uses a shallow concatenation of independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left LMs.
records.quote: This is also in contrast to Peters et al. (2018a) , which uses a shallow concatenation of independently trained left-to-right and right-to-left LMs.

records.claim: CutMix augmentation strategy cuts and pastes patches among training images where the ground truth labels are also mixed proportionally to the area of the patches.

records.claim: When visualized via a scaling curve, emergent abilities show a pattern where performance is near-random until a critical threshold of scale is reached, after which performance increases to substantially above random.

records.claim: The qualitative change associated with emergent abilities is also known as a phase transition.
records.scope_ref: emergent abilities of large language models
records.quote: This qualitative change is also known as a phase transition —a dramatic change in overall behavior that would not have been foreseen by examining smaller-scale systems ( Huberman Hogg, 1987 ) .

records.claim: Using training FLOPs or model parameters as the x-axis produces curves with similar shapes because most dense Transformer language model families have scaled training compute roughly proportionally with model parameters.

records.claim: Pre-training on in-domain unlabeled data can improve performance on downstream tasks.

records.claim: Pre-training BERT on text from research papers improved its performance on scientific tasks.
records.quote: Similar observations have been made in prior work, e.g. Beltagy et al. (2019) found that pre-training BERT on text from research papers improved its performance on scientific tasks.

records.claim: Pre-training on a more diverse data set yielded improvements on downstream tasks.

records.quote: we find that lower-resource tasks like SQuAD work well with a small value of d d whereas higher resource tasks require a large dimensionality to achieve reasonable performance.

records.claim: Gradual unfreezing caused a minor degradation in performance across all tasks, though it did provide some speedup during fine-tuning.
records.quote: We found that gradual unfreezing caused a minor degradation in performance across all tasks, though it did provide some speedup during fine-tuning.

records.claim: Denoising objectives outperformed language modeling and deshuffling for pre-training.
records.quote: Overall, the most significant difference in performance we observed was that denoising objectives outperformed language modeling and deshuffling for pre-training.

records.claim: There was no remarkable difference across the many variants of the denoising objectives explored.
records.quote: We did not observe a remarkable difference across the many variants of the denoising objectives we explored.

records.claim: Different objectives or parameterizations can lead to different sequence lengths and thus different training speeds.
records.quote: However, different objectives (or parameterizations of objectives) can lead to different sequence lengths and thus different training speeds.

records.claim: Choosing among the denoising objectives considered should mainly be done according to their computational cost.
records.quote: This implies that choosing among the denoising objectives we considered here should mainly be done according to their computational cost.

records.claim: Additional exploration of objectives similar to those considered may not lead to significant gains for the tasks and model considered.
records.quote: Our results also suggest that additional exploration of objectives similar to the ones we consider here may not lead to significant gains for the tasks and model we consider.

records.claim: It may be fortuitous to explore entirely different ways of leveraging unlabeled data.
records.quote: Instead, it may be fortuitous to explore entirely different ways of leveraging unlabeled data.

records.claim: Larger models tend to perform better.
records.quote: An unsurprising but important result from our study is that larger models tend to perform better.

records.claim: Scaling up may continue to be a promising way to achieve better performance because hardware is getting cheaper and more powerful.
records.quote: The fact that the hardware used for running these models is continually getting cheaper and more powerful suggests that scaling up may continue to be a promising way to achieve better performance ( Sutton, 2019 ) .

records.claim: Using a smaller or less expensive model is helpful in applications like client-side inference or federated learning.
records.quote: However, it will always be the case that there are applications and scenarios where using a smaller or less expensive model is helpful, for example when performing client-side inference or federated learning ( Konečnỳ et al., 2015 ; Konečnỳ et al., 2016 ) .

records.claim: A beneficial use of transfer learning is the possibility of attaining good performance on low-resource tasks.
records.quote: Relatedly, one beneficial use of transfer learning is the possibility of attaining good performance on low-resource tasks.

records.claim: Low-resource applications often have limited access to computational resources which can incur additional costs.
records.quote: As a result, we advocate for research on methods that achieve stronger performance with cheaper models so that transfer learning can be applied where it will have the most impact.

records.claim: The authors advocate for research on methods that achieve stronger performance with cheaper models.
records.quote: As a result, we advocate for research on methods that achieve stronger performance with cheaper models so that transfer learning can be applied where it will have the most impact.

records.claim: Training the model to denoise corrupted spans of text may not be a very efficient way to teach the model general-purpose knowledge.
records.quote: We suspect that this simplistic technique may not be a very efficient way to teach the model general-purpose knowledge.

records.claim: It would be useful to attain good fine-tuning performance without needing to train models on 1 trillion tokens of text first.
records.quote: More concretely, it would be useful to be able to attain good fine-tuning performance without needing to train our models on 1 1 trillion tokens of text first.

records.claim: Pre-training on unlabeled in-domain data can improve performance on downstream tasks.
records.quote: We observed that pre-training on unlabeled in-domain data can improve performance on downstream tasks ( Section   3.4 ).

records.claim: It would be useful to formulate a more rigorous notion of the “similarity” between the pre-training and downstream tasks.
records.quote: It would be useful to formulate a more rigorous notion of the “similarity” between the pre-training and downstream tasks, so that we could make more principled choices about what source of unlabeled data to use.

records.claim: English-only pre-training did not achieve state-of-the-art results on the translation tasks studied.
records.quote: We were disappointed to find that English-only pre-training did not achieve state-of-the-art results on the translation tasks we studied.

records.claim: The authors are interested in investigating language-agnostic models that can perform a given NLP task with good performance regardless of the text’s language.
records.quote: To address these issues, we are interested in further investigating language-agnostic models, i.e. models that can perform a given NLP task with good performance regardless of the text’s language.

records.claim: The T5 model nearly matched human-level performance on the SuperGLUE benchmark.
records.quote: We are happy to be able to continue this trend, for example by nearly matching human-level performance on the SuperGLUE benchmark, a task specifically designed to be difficult for modern transfer-learning pipelines.

records.quote: Our results stem from the combination of a straightforward and unified text-to-text framework, our new C4 data set, and insights from our systematic study.

records.quote: The objective of the scaling laws from Hoffmann et al. (2022) is to determine how to best scale the dataset and model sizes for a particular training compute budget.
